security_implications: This chunk defines the sparse FSM encoding for the key sideload controller. The SEC_CM comment explicitly marks it as a hardware countermeasure against synthesis optimizations that would weaken the resistance to fault injection. If the sparse property is not maintained or if illegal states are not detected, an attacker could flip FSM bits to bypass key wipe/stop and leak secret keys. The declared signals (keys_en, data_truncated) suggest subsequent key data handling, so an unprotected FSM could directly expose key material.
